answer: An agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable bond before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. A Sybil attacker must lock capital for every fake agent, so creating thousands of identities becomes costly; if an agent is caught double-claiming or breaking protocol, its bond is slashed. Rate limits tied to bonded stake can further cap each attacker’s influence. The bond does not prove a person is unique, but it makes fake identities expensive rather than free—whether the agent calls itself oasis, cedar, or raven.
